newsitem.title: USA: Apple debuts software distribution site.
newsitem.headline: Apple debuts software distribution site.

text.p: Apple Computer Inc on Wednesday unveiled the first part of an Internet commerce strategy by opening a World Wide Web site where customers can get Macintosh software.
For a $19.95 annual subscription fee, customers can download hundreds of utility programmes, bug fixes and printer software from the Apple Club site, Apple executives said.

Apple also is considering selling commercial Macintosh software through the site, which would help Apple get around retailers that are becoming increasingly reluctant to carry Macintosh software on their shelves.
The site is part of a larger Internet commerce strategy Apple will unfold during the next few months, said Philippe Bouissou, Apple's director of Internet services.

"We are studying how we can better serve our customers through the Internet," Bouissou said. In the future, Apple Club "might be another way to shop for Macintosh software, but it won't replace" retailers' Apple software business, he said.
For now, Apple Club offers shareware - the freely distributed software that lets customers customise their Macs or improve the machines' performance.

The shareware available on Apple Club is also available at Apple's Web site for free, but Apple Club offers faster downloads and electronic newsletters for Macintosh software developers, Bouissou said.

In the past few years, Apple has seen software based on Microsoft Corp's Windows standard crowd out retail shelf space for Macintosh software. That has led many potential PC customers to buy Windows-based personal computers instead of a Mac.

An online software distribution strategy would help Apple increase the availability of Macintosh software. But it also could hurt the businesses of dedicated Mac retailers, pushing them to pull even more Mac software off their shelves.
Bouissou declined to give details about Apple's Internet commerce strategy. He said not hurting retailers' businesses is a priority.
The company will unveil other parts of its strategy in the northern spring, he said.
